---
title: "try() around a function does not protect its calls"
ref: FUN-12
categories: [Functions]
impact: cryptique
attendu: "a result for each element, with the error caught for `\"a\"`"
versions: "All"
source: "Slack ThinkR (2019)"
---

::: {.piege}
```{r}
values <- list(1, "a", 3)
lapply(values, try(log))
```
:::

## Why

`try()` evaluates the expression you give it, and only that one. Here, that expression is `log`, the name of the function: evaluating it merely returns the function, with no error. `lapply()` therefore receives a bare `log`, and the call `log("a")` fails with no protection at all.

The loop stops at the first faulty element, while the `try()` seems to promise the opposite.

## The fix

Put `try()` inside an anonymous function, around the call itself.

::: {.piege}
```{r}
results <- lapply(values, function(p) {
  try(log(p), silent = TRUE)
})
vapply(results, FUN = inherits, FUN.VALUE = logical(1), what = "try-error")
```
:::
